name: Oiled (hardwax oil)
process: After sanding, a hardwax oil (drying plant oils with waxes and driers) is spread very thinly along the grain, two coats, with no sanding between. It soaks into the surface cells and pores and cures to a microporous, water-repellent layer, not a film: the white scatter of the bare surface goes, the colour deepens and the fibre highlight shows, under a soft sheen. It is renewed by re-oiling where it wears.

ingredients.text: Natural plant oils (sunflower, soybean, thistle) and waxes, paraffin, siccatives and water-repellent additives; in dearomatised white spirit.
ingredients.source: Osmo Holz und Color GmbH & Co. KG, Product Information | Interior: Polyx-Oil Original, https://int.osmo.com/fileadmin/media/pim_assets/pim_file_36247.pdf

sheens.text: Clear grades: glossy (3011), satin (3032), matt (3062), semi-matt (3065).
sheens.source: Osmo Holz und Color GmbH & Co. KG, Product Information | Interior: Polyx-Oil Original, https://int.osmo.com/fileadmin/media/pim_assets/pim_file_36247.pdf

resistance.text: Resistant to wine, beer, cola, coffee, tea, fruit juice, milk and water to DIN 68861-1A; microporous; will not crack, peel, flake or blister.
resistance.source: Osmo Holz und Color GmbH & Co. KG, Product Information | Interior: Polyx-Oil Original, https://int.osmo.com/fileadmin/media/pim_assets/pim_file_36247.pdf

mechanism.text: A clear finish with an index close to the cell wall's removes the first, irregular interface, so bare wood's white surface scatter goes, colour deepens and the subsurface fibre highlight appears.
mechanism.source: Marschner, S.R., Westin, S.H., Arbree, A. & Moon, J.T. (2005) Measuring and modeling the appearance of finished wood. ACM Transactions on Graphics 24(3), 727-734, https://doi.org/10.1145/1073204.1073254 (https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~srm/publications/SG05-wood-lr.pdf)

optics.surfaceSpecular: The cured oil-wax surface gives a weak dielectric reflection (F0 of a few per cent) with a broad lobe for matt and satin grades; see unverified for its index.

museumChoiceSource: plan/proposals/salon-interior/canvas/Light.dc.html (approved Salon interior proposal) ('The floor: warm oak, no glare'); plan/canvas/MaterialsOther.dc.html, section 'D · The oak, and what it carries' ('Oiled')
photograph: A low, soft sheen that follows the grain; no plastic film on top; pores still open to the touch.
Traffic paths duller and paler on a floor until it is re-oiled.

unverified.reason: Drying oils and waxes lie near 1.44-1.48 in handbooks (for example linseed oil about 1.478, beeswax 1.443-1.449 in the CRC Handbook as quoted by MFA CAMEO), but those pages could not be opened.
Would follow as 0.033-0.038 from the unverified index.
The darkening of oak by this oil (delta L*) was not measured in a source read.
